title: standardize-reauth-metadata-and-async-closer-facade-cross-sdk-v1.28.0
author: Priya Menon
body:
Context and motivation: Multi-SDK teams continue to drift on small but breaking ergonomics around reauth metadata, session hints, and stream shutdown semantics. This PR standardizes the "reauth hint" metadata contract that the client SDK surfaces to the runtime and introduces a small, explicit ClosableAsyncIterator / StreamHandle API in the TypeScript SDK (mirrored in Go/Python in companion PRs) to make graceful stream teardown and in-flight token handoff deterministic. The goal is parity across TS/Py/Go for token hinting + a small ergonomic upgrade for consumers that need ordered shutdown (safely drain, optionally prefetch/prime next token) while preserving backwards compatibility.

This description contains the full change list, commits, CI summary, review conversation, and merge notes below.

What changed (high level): 1) Add a lightweight 'reauth-hint' header field in client requests and a typed ReauthHint interface in the SDKs so adapters and gateways can pick up a canonical hint (preferred expiry_offset_ms, preferred_credential_chain_id). 2) Introduce ClosableAsyncIterator and StreamHandle types in the TS SDK: close(reason?) returns a promise that resolves when the iterator drains and releases underlying resources; a gracefulClose option exists for draining vs abort. 3) Expose a new client config field 'credentialHinting: { enabled:true|false }' defaulting to true to allow gradual rollout. 4) Add integration tests across Node/Browser bundles that assert handshake includes reauth-hint and that close() triggers socket drain rather than immediate abort. 5) Bump package to v1.28.0 and add a short migration note.

Compatibility and migration notes: credentialHinting defaults to true so existing consumers see no behavioral change. The new types are additive; existing AsyncIterator consumers will continue to work. The reauth metadata keys are optional on the wire - runtime will ignore when missing. See release_notes for tips.

Checklist: - [x] Spec and Linear ticket (ENG-12291) linked - [x] TS SDK implementation - [x] E2E tests (Node + Browser) - [x] Companion PRs in redwood-sdk-go and redwood-sdk-python prepared - [x] Docs snippet and migration note - [x] Version bump and CHANGELOG entry

Related: Linear ENG-12291, ENG-12318; companion PRs: redwood-sdk-go#274590 (credential-dampener), redwood-sdk-python#381207 (session-lease-deterministic-retries).
commits: a3f9b72  Add ReauthHint type, credentialHinting config and basic serializers
b8d7c5e  Implement ClosableAsyncIterator + StreamHandle and unit tests
c2e1d4a  Add integration test for Node/browser handshake and graceful close
e4f2b11  Bump version to v1.28.0 and add changelog/migration notes
changed_files_summary: src/client/config.ts: add credentialHinting config and defaults
rollup.config.ts: ensure browser bundle exports ClosableAsyncIterator
ci_checks_summary: Initial run: 1 flaky e2e failed on Node (socket drain timeout) — rerun passed. Unit tests: pass. Lint: pass. Bundle size check: pass. Coverage: 92.3%.
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Nice small surface. One question: the reauth hint currently exposes expiry_offset_ms; how should SDKs compute that safely in low-resolution timers? Suggest we document recommended jitter/rounding.
Hannah Lee: Please add a short internal note explaining how this interacts with the Dedicated routing fallback: we need to ensure hints are stripped for customers who opt-out at the routing layer.
Marcus Chen: The StreamHandle API looks good. Can we add an optional onClose hook so applications can run a cleanup after drain?
author_responses: Priya Menon: @Diego added explanation + code comment recommending Math.max(0, expiryMs - 1500) rounding in src/auth/reauth_hint.ts and an integration test to assert non-negative hint values.

Priya Menon: @Hannah noted in docs/migrations.md that routing layers may remove reauth meta; credentialHinting flag allows clients to opt out. Also added an internal-only flag to strip hints at gateway when configured.
Priya Menon: @Marcus added optional onClose hook to StreamHandle and unit tests that assert it is invoked after drain completes.
release_notes:
- Add ReauthHint metadata contract (optional).
- Introduce ClosableAsyncIterator/StreamHandle to allow graceful drain and deterministic teardown.
- Add credentialHinting config (default: enabled).
- Bump TypeScript SDK to v1.28.0.
Migration: Most consumers require no changes; see docs/migrations.md for examples on using StreamHandle.close() and opt-out configuration.
